title: Expired clock_nanosleep fast path bypasses clock validation
mechanism: do_clock_nanosleep reads the clock and returns 0 for an absolute deadline already in the past before it reaches the match that rejects clocks without sleep support, so clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, TIMER_ABSTIME, past) succeeds instead of failing with EOPNOTSUPP.
contract: clock_nanosleep(2): sleeping against a clock the kernel cannot sleep on fails with ENOTSUP (EOPNOTSUPP, 95 on x86-64), and Linux returns it for CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW even when the absolute deadline has passed.
observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): the raw syscall returns 0 for CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW with TIMER_ABSTIME and deadline {0, 1}.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for clock_nanosleep_rawpast, libc_clock_error. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Raw syscall (-1/errno) and glibc (positive return) conventions differ, which the libc_clock_error control separates. Only CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW is probed.
